localChanges: chore: lock the engine packages that put a city's production on Auto

log: `civ1-city:city/building-complete/auto` and `civ1-city:city/building-cancelled/auto` start what a city on Auto needs most (`core-city-build`'s `rankBuildItems` over `BuildPriority`) when its build is complete or can no longer be built. `lib/autoBuild` limits the choice to improvements and Wonders, never units. `civ1-city:city/captured/stop-auto` takes a captured city off Auto. Needs core-city-build 0.1.13 (civ-clone/web-renderer#194).

`civ1-city:player/turn-start/auto-build` runs `lib/autoBuild` for each of the player's cities at the start of its turn, after production. Until now a city only chose on `BuildingComplete` / `BuildingCancelled`, so a city put on Auto before its player knew any improvement worth building sat on nothing for good (civ-clone/web-renderer#194).

The filter only left out units, so anything else a city can build, such as a spaceship part, could be chosen once a `BuildPriority` scored it. Allow `CityImprovement` (Wonders included) instead. Spaceship parts are left to a space race strategy (civ-clone/web-renderer#376).
The test's `BuildPriority` and `Build` callbacks now take `IBuildable`, so it type-checks under ts-mocha.

`Rules/City/build-priority.ts` registers a `BuildPriority` for each Civ1 improvement from the city's yields and size: a Granary for a starving city (and a little for one of size 3+ with 1 Food or less to spare), an Aqueduct near size 10 (sooner with Food to spare), a Temple, Colosseum and Cathedral for unhappy citizens, a Marketplace and Bank for gold and luxuries, a Library and University for science, a Courthouse for corruption, a Factory for shields and the plants only beside a Factory. The everyday improvements (Granary, Temple, Marketplace, Library, Courthouse, Bank, University) score at least 0.1, so a city on Auto always has one to build. Each is weighed against its upkeep, as a share of the city's gold. Barracks and City Walls score only while a unit or city of a player the owner isn't at peace with is within 5 tiles, and then above everything else: Civ1 has no declared war, so having met isn't enough. `Rules/City/cost.ts` exports its upkeep tables and an `upkeep()` helper for this, with no change to the costs. Needs core-city-build 0.1.13 (civ-clone/web-renderer#194).

`Corruption` yields are negative, so the total was never 2 or more and a Courthouse only ever got the everyday floor. Negate the total, and build the test's yields the way `civ1-city` does (a positive amount, whose `value()` is negative), which the old test had backwards.

`Rules/City/build-priority.ts` gives a Wonder a `BuildPriority` of 1.5 in a city making 5 shields or more, when it isn't obsolete, would do something for its player (the Lighthouse and Magellan's only with ships; never the Manhattan Project), and none of the player's other cities is building it. Needs core-city-build 0.1.13 (civ-clone/web-renderer#194).

`CityBuild` gains `auto()` / `setAuto()` (saved as `_auto`; a build restored from an older save reads as not on Auto). `BuildPriority` rules score `(cityBuild, item, yields)`, with the city's yields worked out once per ranking; `lib/rankBuildItems` adds the matches, weighs them, drops anything at 0 or below and orders the rest highest first, then cheaper, then by name. `lib/autoBuild` starts the top-ranked item for a city on Auto that is building nothing. Rulesets act on the flag from their `BuildingComplete` / `BuildingCancelled` rules (civ-clone/web-renderer#194).
`localeCompare` follows the host's locale, so two clients could order equally scored, equally priced items differently. Compare by UTF-16 code unit instead, so the choice is the same on every client.

`buildItemInCity`'s random pick, weighed by the leader's `BuildWeight`, still decides between a unit and an improvement. When it lands on an improvement, or on nothing, the city builds the one `rankImprovements` puts first: core-city-build's `rankBuildItems` over the ruleset's `BuildPriority` rules, among the improvements it can finish within the policy's turns, weighed by `BuildWeight`. With nothing ranked, the pick stands. Barracks and City Walls go through the ranking, which only wants them with an enemy near. A city's yields are worked out once per choice and shared with `netShields`. Under a leader with no preference the ranking is the one a city on Auto uses; Ideology weighs improvements against Wonders.

Arena, 80 games of 150 turns against master: nothing at |t| >= 2 (score -0.36, t -1.1; advances -0.07, t -0.8). The choice is reached about 21 times a game (civ-clone/web-renderer#194). Needs core-city-build 0.1.13.

As civ-clone/web-renderer#194 specified: the top-ranked finishable improvement comes first, and the leader-weighted random pick only when nothing ranks. Before, a random pick that landed on a unit stood, so a starving city could keep building Warriors with a Granary ranked.

The random pick rarely runs now, so a Militaristic leader's lean towards units (#157) shows mostly in the quotas. Arena (80 games, against e972402): score +0.02 (t 0.0), units -0.57 (t -2.1), improvements +0.33 (t 3.8). Ranking units by need, so the lean returns through `BuildWeight` in the same ranking, is civ-clone/web-renderer#378. The #157 random-pick tests now set up a city that needs nothing.
